[2] Inner Edge Habitable Zone Limits Around Main Sequence Stars: Cloudy Estimates

2024-01-00

Understanding the limits of rocky planet habitability is one of the key goals of current and future exoplanet characterization efforts. An intrinsic concept of rocky planet habitability is the Habitable Zone. To date, the most widely used estimates of the Habitable Zone are based on cloud-free, one-dimensional (vertical) radiative-convective climate model calculations. However, recent three-dimensional global climate modeling efforts have revealed that rocky planet habitability is strongly impacted by radiative cloud feedbacks, where computational expense and model limitations can prevent these tools from exploring the limits of habitability across the full range of parameter space. We leverage a patchy cloud one-dimensional radiative-convective climate model with parameterized cloud microphysics to investigate Inner Edge limits to the Habitable Zone for main sequence stars ($T_{\rm eff}$ = 2600 -7200K). We find that Inner Edge limits to the Habitable Zone can be 3.3 and 4.7 times closer than previous cloud-free estimates for Earth- and super-Earth-sized worlds, respectively, depending on bulk cloud parameters (e.g., fractional cloudiness and sedimentation efficiency). These warm, moist Inner Edge climates are expected to have extensive cloud decks that could mute deep atmosphere spectral features. To aid in rocky planet characterization studies, we identify the potential of using $\rm{CO_{\rm 2}}$ absorption features in transmission spectroscopy as a means of quantifying cloud deck height and cloud sedimentation efficiency. Moist greenhouse climates may represent key yet poorly understood states of habitable planets for which continued study will uncover new insights into the search and characterization of habitable worlds.

[2] 主序星周围宜居带内缘的限制：云的估算

理解岩石行星宜居性的极限是当前和未来系外行星表征工作的关键目标之一。岩石行星宜居性的核心概念是宜居带。目前，最广泛使用的宜居带估算基于无云、一维（垂直）辐射-对流气候模型计算。然而，近期三维全球气候模拟显示，岩石行星的宜居性受到辐射云反馈的强烈影响，而计算成本和模型局限性可能阻碍这些工具在全参数空间范围内探索宜居性的极限。我们利用带有参数化云微物理的斑块云一维辐射-对流气候模型，研究主序星（$T_{\rm eff}$ = 2600 - 7200K）宜居带内缘的极限。我们发现，对于类地和超级地球大小的行星，宜居带内缘极限可分别比先前无云估算近 3.3 和 4.7 倍，具体取决于云的整体参数（如云量分数和沉降效率）。这些温暖、潮湿的内缘气候预计会有广泛的云层，可能削弱深层大气的光谱特征。为辅助岩石行星表征研究，我们提出利用透射光谱中的 $\rm{CO_{\rm 2}}$ 吸收特征来量化云层高度和云沉降效率的潜力。潮湿温室气候可能代表了关键但尚不充分理解的宜居行星状态，持续研究将为宜居世界的搜寻和表征带来新见解。

[3] Cloud Radiative Influences On The Edges of Habitability

2025-01-00

True occurrence rates for "exo-Earth" candidates remain uncertain due to survey completeness issues, but synthesis studies suggest they are harbored by 2-12% of the stars in the Milky Way galaxy. Characterization of suitable exo-Earth candidates, through transit and or direct imaging studies, remains a primary motivator of exoplanet astronomy. However, full characterization of exo-Earth candidates requires a deep understanding of their underlying physical and chemical atmospheric properties, as well the ability to connect these properties to observations. The radiative properties of planetary atmospheres are foundational to observed spectral characteristics and are intrinsic to surface climate characteristics. Following basic atmospheric composition, clouds and aerosols all but control the radiative properties of the atmospheres in which they arise, and thus, may have profound effects on observational properties and climate characteristics. Much like the influence clouds and aerosols have on the climate and observational characteristics of our own planet, it is expected that clouds and aerosols are intrinsic to the thermo-chemical feedbacks that regulate the climates and observational properties of potential exo-Earth candidates. As the observational methods, resources, and instrumentation allocated towards exo-Earth characterization studies continually improve, so too must the planetary climate models used to study, predict, and characterize these worlds. We present a novel, one-dimensional radiative-convective terrestrial planet climate model that self-consistently computes parameterized cloud microphysics, cloud optical properties, and cloud radiative effects through a thoroughly tested, chemical equilibrium cloud model that explicitly treats condensation and sedimentation processes. We leverage this robust climate model to compute cloud-driven radiative effects and spectral signatures for a range of climate states, spanning the newly defined boundaries of the Habitable Zone—from warm, moist super-Earths at the Inner Edge to cold, glacier-covered worlds at the Outer Edge.

[3] 云辐射对宜居带边缘的影响

由于巡天完备性问题，“类地系外行星”候选体的真实出现率仍不确定，但综合研究表明它们存在于银河系2-12%的恒星周围。通过凌星和直接成像等方法对合适的类地系外行星候选体进行特性刻画，仍然是系外行星天文学的主要动力。然而，全面刻画类地系外行星候选体需要深入理解其基本物理和化学大气属性，并能够将这些属性与观测联系起来。行星大气的辐射特性是观测到的光谱特征的基础，并且与表面气候特性密切相关。在基本大气成分之外，云和气溶胶几乎主导了它们所处大气的辐射特性，因此可能对观测属性和气候特性产生深远影响。正如云和气溶胶对地球气候和观测特性的影响一样，预计它们也是调节潜在类地系外行星气候和观测属性的热化学反馈的内在组成部分。随着用于类地系外行星刻画研究的观测方法、资源和仪器不断提升，用于研究、预测和刻画这些世界的行星气候模型也必须不断进步。我们提出了一种新颖的一维辐射-对流类地行星气候模型，该模型通过经过充分测试的化学平衡云模型自洽地计算参数化的云微物理、云光学性质和云辐射效应，并显式处理凝结和沉降过程。我们利用这一稳健的气候模型，计算了由云驱动的辐射效应和光谱特征，涵盖了新定义的宜居带边界范围内的多种气候状态——从内缘的温暖潮湿超级地球到外缘的寒冷冰川覆盖世界。

[4] Exoplanet weather and climate regimes with clouds and thermal ionospheres. A model grid study in support of large-scale observational campaigns

2023-03-00

Context. Gaseous exoplanets are the targets that enable us to explore fundamentally our understanding of planetary physics and chemistry. With observational efforts moving from the discovery into the characterisation mode, systematic campaigns that cover large ranges of global stellar and planetary parameters will be needed to disentangle the diversity of exoplanets and their atmospheres that all are affected by their formation and evolutionary paths. Ideally, the spectral range includes the high-energy (ionisation) and the low-energy (phase-transitions) processes as they carry complementary information of the same object. <BR /> Aims: We aim to uncover cloud formation trends and globally changing chemical regimes into which gas-giant exoplanets may fall due to the host star's effect on the thermodynamic structure of their atmospheres. We aim to examine the emergence of an ionosphere as indicator for potentially asymmetric magnetic field effects on these atmospheres. We aim to provide input for exoplanet missions such as JWST, PLATO, and Ariel, as well as potential UV missions ARAGO, PolStar, or POLLUX on LUVOIR. <BR /> Methods: Pre-calculated 3D GCMs for M, K, G, F host stars are the input for our kinetic cloud model for the formation of nucleation seeds, the growth to macroscopic cloud particles and their evaporation, gravitational settling, element conservation and gas chemistry. <BR /> Results: Gaseous exoplanets fall broadly into three classes: i) cool planets with homogeneous cloud coverage, ii) intermediate temperature planets with asymmetric dayside cloud coverage, and iii) ultra-hot planets without clouds on the dayside. In class ii), the dayside cloud patterns are shaped by the wind flow and irradiation. Surface gravity and planetary rotation have little effect. For a given effective temperature, planets around K dwarfs are rotating faster compared to G dwarfs leading to larger cloud inhomogeneities in the fast rotating case. Extended atmosphere profiles suggest the formation of mineral haze in form of metal-oxide clusters (e.g. (TiO<SUB>2</SUB>)<SUB>N</SUB>). <BR /> Conclusions: The dayside cloud coverage is the tell-tale sign for the different planetary regimes and their resulting weather and climate appearance. Class (i) is representative of planets with a very homogeneous cloud particle size and material compositions across the globe (e.g., HATS-6b, NGTS-1b), classes (ii, e.g., WASP-43b, HD 209458b) and (iii, e.g., WASP-121b, WP 0137b) have a large day-night divergence of the cloud properties. The C/O ratio is, hence, homogeneously affected in class (i), but asymmetrically in class (ii) and (iii). The atmospheres of class (i) and (ii) planets are little affected by thermal ionisation, but class (iii) planets exhibit a deep ionosphere on the dayside. Magnetic coupling will therefore affect different planets differently and will be more efficient on the more extended, cloud-free dayside. How the ionosphere connects atmospheric mass loss at the top of the atmosphere with deep atmospheric layers need to be investigated to coherently interpret high resolution observations of ultra-hot planets.

背景：气态系外行星是我们探索行星物理和化学基本规律的关键目标。随着观测工作从发现阶段转向特性研究，需要覆盖广泛恒星和行星参数的大规模系统性观测，以厘清系外行星及其大气的多样性，这些多样性均受到其形成和演化路径的影响。理想情况下，光谱范围应涵盖高能（电离）和低能（相变）过程，因为它们为同一目标提供互补信息。<BR /> 目标：我们旨在揭示云形成趋势及气态巨行星因母星对其大气热力学结构影响而可能出现的全球化学变化模式。我们还希望研究电离层的出现，作为大气中潜在不对称磁场效应的指示。我们致力于为JWST、PLATO、Ariel等系外行星任务，以及未来可能的紫外任务ARAGO、PolStar或LUVOIR上的POLLUX等提供参考。<BR /> 方法：以M、K、G、F型母星的预计算三维全球环流模型（GCM）为输入，结合动力学云模型，模拟成核种子的形成、云粒子的生长与蒸发、重力沉降、元素守恒和气体化学过程。<BR /> 结果：气态系外行星大致可分为三类：i）具有均匀云覆盖的冷行星，ii）具有不对称昼面云覆盖的中等温度行星，iii）昼面无云的超热行星。在第ii类中，昼面云分布受风场和辐射影响。表面重力和行星自转影响较小。在相同有效温度下，K矮星周围的行星自转更快，导致快速自转情况下云的不均匀性更大。大气延展剖面显示，可能形成以金属氧化物簇（如（TiO<SUB>2</SUB>)<SUB>N</SUB>）为代表的矿物雾霾。<BR /> 结论：昼面云覆盖是区分不同行星大气模式及其天气和气候表现的关键特征。第(i)类代表全球云粒子大小和成分高度均匀的行星（如HATS-6b、NGTS-1b），第(ii)类（如WASP-43b、HD 209458b）和第(iii)类（如WASP-121b、WP 0137b）则表现出昼夜云性质的巨大差异。C/O比在第(i)类中均匀受影响，而在第(ii)和(iii)类中则表现出不对称性。第(i)和(ii)类行星的大气受热电离影响较小，但第(iii)类行星的昼面存在深厚电离层。因此，磁场耦合对不同行星的影响不同，在更为延展、无云的昼面更为高效。电离层如何将大气顶层的大气逃逸与深层大气连接起来，需要进一步研究，以便对超热行星的高分辨率观测进行一致性解释。

In recent years, many different types of exoplanets have been discovered. Understanding the conditions and chemical cycles present on these diverse worlds will be enabled by spectroscopic characterization of their atmospheres. Terrestrial-like exoplanets can contain many chemical species, yet only a few have the distinct spectral features and atmospheric abundance to be detectable, viz., CO2, CO, CH4, H2O, H2, O2, O3, NH3, H2O2, and C2H2. O2 and O3 can be produced abiotically by photolysis of CO2 and preferential escape of H and biotically in the presence of life. Around G-type stars, CO2 photolysis by FUV radiation is balanced by recombination reactions dependent on water abundance. Planets orbiting stars with more FUV radiation could be depleted in water due to prolonged high FUV exposure. For these exoplanets, a catalytic cycle relying on H2O2 photolysis can maintain a CO2 atmosphere. This cycle breaks down for low atmospheric hydrogen mixing ratios, causing a significant fraction of the atmospheric CO2 to be converted to CO and O2 on timescale of ~1 Myr (Gao et al., 2015), especially on planets in the habitable zones of K- and M- type stars. The abundances of other species are determined by planetary atmospheric conditions during formation and subsequent evolution. This evolution is largely dependent upon the FUV-NUV radiation ratio from the parent star, the balance of CO2 photolysis against recombination via reactions that depend on water abundance, and various catalytic chemical cycles characterized via atmospheric composition, dynamics, energetics, and chemical behavior. <P />The 1-D photochemical models previously used to understand these processes are inconsistent due to their limited capabilities, producing conflicting results under similar circumstances. We propose to estimate conditions for the state and evolution of CO2 dominated terrestrial-type exoplanets orbiting around M-dwarf type stars with varying star/planet distances to determine abundances for key observable species by considering the effects of 3-dimensional GCM heating/cooling, dynamics, and HOx and ClOx photochemistry and catalytic cycles. Using the output from this modeling, we will create spectra for likely detectable species using state of the art radiative transfer models. Specifically, we will: <P />1. Characterize CO2 dominated exoplanetary atmospheric dayside heating budgets of EUV-NIR heating and CO2 15-μm cooling in a 3-D GCM model allowing a self-consistent quantification of the associated photochemistry and climatological upper atmospheric circulation using existing validated published models for planets with CO2 dominated atmospheres orbiting different M-dwarf stars. We will target potential dense CO2 dominated atmospheres for terrestrial sized planets that are scheduled for JWST Cycle 1 observations. <P />2. Assess the influence of HOx, ClOx, and SOx photochemistry and catalytic cycles and heating/cooling in 3-D GCM modeling to determine the distribution of key species abundances for these types of planetary atmospheres. <P />3. Use the results from Objectives 1 and 2 to determine synthetic spectra of LTE and non-LTE emissions using radiative transfer models. These synthentic spectra will be used to determine the potential observability of exoplanet atmospheric non-LTE emissions (i.e. flourescence) for the most likely detectable species. <P />The results our study will be helpful for interpreting and planning forthcoming JWST, ARIEL, and other future observations.

[1] The strange case of Na I in the atmosphere of HD 209458 b. Reconciling low- and high-resolution spectroscopic observations

2022-01-00

<BR /> Aims: We aim to investigate the origin of the discrepant results reported in the literature about the presence of Na I in the atmosphere of HD 209458 b, based on low- and high-resolution transmission spectroscopy. <BR /> Methods: We generated synthetic planetary atmosphere models and we compared them with the transmission light curves and spectra observed in previous studies. Our models account for the stellar limb-darkening and Rossiter-McLaughlin (RM) effects, and contemplate various possible scenarios for the planetary atmosphere. <BR /> Results: We reconciled the discrepant results by identifying a range of planetary atmospheres that are consistent with previous low- and high-resolution spectroscopic observations. Either both datasets are interpreted as consistent with a total absence of Na I in the planetary atmosphere (with Hubble Space Telescope data being affected by limb darkening), or the terminator temperature of HD 209458 b has to have an upper limit of about 1000 K. In particular, we find that 1D transmission spectra with lower-than-equilibrium temperatures can also explain the previously reported detection of absorption signal at low resolution due to differential transit depth in adjacent bands, while the cores of the Na I D lines may be masked by the strong RM signal seen at high resolution. We also rule out high-altitude clouds, which would otherwise mask the absorption signal at low resolution, as the source of the discrepancies. <BR /> Conclusions: This work highlights the synergies between different observing techniques, specifically low- and high-resolution spectroscopy, to fully characterise transiting exoplanet systems.

However, many of its atmospheric constraints remain debatable. While Hubble Space Telescope (HST) observations suggested a highly subsolar metallicity, recent JWST NIRCam observations by Q. Xue et al. constrained a supersolar metallicity with highly subsolar C/O. The overall best-fitting model with free retrievals (<inline-formula> <mml:math><mml:msubsup><mml:mrow><mml:mi>χ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>red</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msubsup></mml:math> </inline-formula> = 1.21) constrains its metallicity and C/O to be highly subsolar, while equilibrium chemistry and grid retrievals (<inline-formula> <mml:math><mml:msubsup><mml:mrow><mml:mi>χ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mi>red</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msubsup></mml:math> </inline-formula> = 1.27 and 1.30, respectively) are consistent with solar values using Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS)+WFC3+NIRCam observations. The retrieved abundances of H<SUB>2</SUB>O and CO<SUB>2</SUB> are almost 3 orders of magnitude lower (highly subsolar) with STIS+WFC3+NIRCam compared to just NIRCam, using free retrievals. NIRCam observations alone also result in misleading constraints on metallicity and C/O, with equilibrium chemistry and grid retrieval. We find that the model choice of varying C/H or O/H to vary the C/O in equilibrium chemistry retrievals leads to different metallicity constraints with NIRCam, but similar constraints with STIS+WFC3+NIRCam. We conclude that NIRCam observations alone can lead to overestimation of abundances for exoplanet atmospheres and, therefore, should be used in combination with UV/optical and near-infrared observations to obtain robust constraints on abundances, C/O, and metallicity. In particular, even though we can detect the CO<SUB>2</SUB> feature with just NIRCam, we cannot constrain its abundances robustly without the optical baseline.

WASP-121 b has been established as a benchmark ultrahot Jupiter, serving as a laboratory for the atmospheric chemistry and dynamics of strongly irradiated extrasolar gas giants. Transmission spectroscopy offers an invaluable opportunity to characterize the atmospheres of exoplanets. We present new ground-based optical transmission spectra of the hot Jupiter HD 189733b, derived from nine transits observed over a six year time span (2016-2021) using near-simultaneous $u^{\prime} g^{\prime} r^{\prime} i^{\prime} $ broadband observations. We achieve an average (best) precision of 435 (280) ppm by implementing an optical diffuser on the prime focus spectrograph from the 2.3 m Wyoming Infrared Observatory telescope. The data provide new measurements of the apparent planetary radius with respect to the stellar radius, the spectral index of atmospheric opacity, and the time variability of the two quantities. Our results indicate an enhanced spectral slope in the optical regime ≍2.4 times steeper than would be expected from canonical Rayleigh scattering and that is consistent with earlier measurements of a super-Rayleigh slope (SRS). While the effect of stellar activity on the transmission spectrum complicates the measurement of the spectral slope, our multiepoch data set over six years can measure and average over stellar variations, yielding a mean spectral index of -9.9 ± 4.4. The 1200 K equilibrium temperature of HD 189733b places it in a sweet spot for the formation of SRSs and is consistent with vigorously mixing hazes in the atmosphere. Additionally, we find variations in the depth of the lightcurve during two of the transits, explainable as an increase in occulted star spots during June 2021. Although the star is active, the mean level of stellar activity does not seem to vary dramatically over our six years of observations, leading us to conclude that the variability in stellar activity is modest at most.

Advances in modern technology have enabled the characterization of exoplanetary atmospheres, which can be achieved by exploitation of the transmission spectroscopy technique. We performed visible (VIS) and near-infrared (NIR) high-resolution spectroscopic observations of one transit of HD 149026b, a close-in orbit sub-Saturn exoplanet by using the GIARPS configuration at the Telescopio Nazionale Galileo (TNG). We then performed transmission spectroscopy, looking for absorption signals from the planetary atmosphere. We find no evidence for Hα, Na I D2-D1, Mg I, or Li I in the VIS and metastable helium triplet He I(2<SUP>3</SUP>S) in the NIR using a line-by-line approach. The non-detection of HeI is also supported by theoretical simulations. With the use of the cross-correlation technique (CCF), we do not detect Ti I, V I, Cr I, Fe I, or VO in the visible, or indeed CH<SUB>4</SUB>, CO<SUB>2</SUB>, H<SUB>2</SUB>O, HCN, NH<SUB>3</SUB>, or VO in the NIR. Our non-detection of Ti I in the planetary atmosphere is in contrast with a previous detection. We performed injection-retrieval tests, finding that our dataset is sensitive to our Ti I model. The non-detection supports the Ti I cold-trap theory, which is valid for planets with T<SUB>eq</SUB> &lt; 2200 K, such as HD 149026b. Although we do not attribute it directly to the planet, we find a possibly significant Ti I signal that is highly redshifted (≃+20 km s<SUP>−1</SUP> ) with respect to the planetary rest frame. Redshifted signals are also found in the Fe I and Cr I maps. While we can exclude an eccentric orbit as the cause of this redshifted Ti I signal, we investigated the possibility of material accretion falling onto the star ─ which is possibly supported by the presence of strong Li I in the stellar spectrum - but obtained inconclusive results. The analysis of multiple transits datasets could shed more light on this target.

[1] Exploring and Validating Exoplanet Atmospheric Retrievals with Solar System Analog Observations

2023-01-00

Solar system observations that serve as analogs for exoplanet remote sensing data can provide important opportunities to validate ideas and models related to exoplanet environments. Critically, and unlike true exoplanet observations, solar system analog data benefit from available high-quality ground- or orbiter-derived "truth" constraints that enable strong validations of exoplanet data interpretation tools. In this work, we first present a versatile atmospheric retrieval suite, capable of application to reflected light, thermal emission, and transmission observations spanning a broad range of wavelengths and thermochemical conditions. The tool-dubbed rfast-is designed, in part, to enable exoplanet mission concept feasibility studies. Following model validation, the retrieval tool is applied to a range of solar system analog observations for exoplanet environments. Retrieval studies using Earth reflected light observations from NASA's EPOXI mission provide a key proof of concept for exo-Earth direct imaging concept missions under development. Inverse modeling applied to an infrared spectrum of Earth from the Mars Global Surveyor Thermal Emission Spectrometer achieves good constraints on atmospheric gases, including many biosignature gases. Finally, retrieval analysis applied to a transit spectrum of Titan derived from the Cassini Visual and Infrared Mapping Spectrometer provides a proof of concept for interpreting more feature-rich transiting exoplanet observations from NASA's James Webb Space Telescope. In the future, solar system analog observations for exoplanets could be used to verify exoplanet models and parameterizations, and future exoplanet analog observations of any solar system worlds from planetary science missions should be encouraged.

Spectroscopic characterization of imaged exoplanets and brown dwarfs is essential for understanding their atmospheres, formation, and evolution, but such work is challenged by the unavoidably simplified model atmospheres needed to interpret spectra. While most previous work has focused on single or at most a few objects, comparing a large collection of spectra to models can uncover trends in data-model inconsistencies needed to improve model predictions, thereby leading to robust properties from exoplanet and brown dwarf spectra. Therefore, we are conducting a systematic analysis of a valuable but underutilized resource: the numerous high-quality spectra of (directly imaged and free-floating) exoplanets and brown dwarfs already accumulated by the community. Focusing on the cool-temperature end, we have constructed a Bayesian modeling framework using the new Sonora-Bobcat model atmospheres and have applied it to study near-infrared low-resolution spectra of &gt;50 late-T imaged planets and brown dwarfs (≍600-1200K, ≍10-70 MJup) and infer their physical properties (effective temperature, surface gravity, metallicity, radii, mass). By virtue of having such a large sample of high-quality spectra, our analysis identifies the systematic offsets between observed and model spectra as a function of wavelength and physical properties to pinpoint specific shortcomings in model predictions. We have also found that the spectroscopically inferred metallicities, ages, and masses of our sample all considerably deviate from expectations, suggesting the physical and chemical assumptions made within these models need to be improved to fully interpret data. Our work has established a systematic validation of cloudless model atmospheres to date and we discuss extending such analysis to wider temperature and wavelength (e.g., JWST) ranges, as well as finding new planetary-mass and brown dwarf benchmarks, in order to validate ultracool model atmospheres over larger parameter space.

The study of exoplanets atmospheres is one of the most intriguing challenges in exoplanet field nowadays and the High Resolution Spectroscopy (HRS) has recently emerged as one of the leading methods for detecting atomic and molecular species in their atmospheres.Nevertheless extraordinary results have been achieved (Birkby, 2018), HRS alone is not enough. 1D models of the host star have been coupled to HRS observations, but they do not reproduce the complexity of stellar convection mechanism (Chiavassa &amp; Brogi, 2019). On the contrary, 3D Radiative Hydrodynamical (3D RHD) simulations take it into account intrinsically, allowing us to correctly reproduce asymmetric and blue-shifted spectral lines due to the granulation pattern of the stellar disk, which is a very important source of uncertainties (Chiavassa et al. 2017). However, numerical simulations have been computed independently for star and planet so far, while the acquired spectrum contains both the signals. For instance, some molecular species (e.g, CO) form in the same region of the spectrum, thus planetary and stellar spectral lines are completely mixed and overlapped. A next step forward is needed: computing stellar and planetary models together during the planet transit.With our work, we aim at upgrading the already-in-place 3D radiative transfer code Optim3D (Chiavassa et al. 2009) — largely used for stellar purposes so far — to take into account also the exoplanetary contribution and finally carry out a full characterisation of planets and their host stars. I will present the advantages of the simultaneous use of 3D RHD stellar simulations and exoplanet's Global Climate Models (GCMs) in generating unprecedented precise synthetic spectra and the two main reasons why stars and planets' spectra should be computed and interpreted together.

The purpose of this paper is to address the question: Using our knowledge of infrared planetary spectroscopy, what can we learn about the atmospheres of exoplanets? In a first part, a simplified classification of exoplanets, assuming thermochemical equilibrium, is presented, based on their masses and their equilibrium temperatures, in order to propose some possible estimations about their atmospheric composition. In the second part, infrared spectra of planets are discussed, in order to see what lessons can be drawn for exoplanetary spectroscopy. In the last part, we consider the solar system as it would appear from a star located in the ecliptic plane. It first appears that the solar system (except in a few specific cases) would not be seen as a multiple system, because, contrary to many exoplanetary systems, the planets are too far from the Sun and the inclinations of their orbits with respect to the ecliptic plane are too high. Primary transit synthetic spectra of solar system planets are used to discuss the relative merits of transmission and direct emission spectroscopy for probing exoplanetary atmospheres.

2024-11-00

Atmospheric spectroscopy provides a window into the properties of exoplanets. However, the physical interpretation of retrieved data and its implications for the internal properties of exoplanets remains nebulous. This letter addresses three misconceptions held by some atmospheric spectroscopists regarding the connection between observed chemical abundances and theory: (1) Whether atmospheric spectroscopy can provide the bulk atmospheric chemistry, (2) whether it can identify if a planet is cloudless, and (3) whether atmospheric evaporation arguments can be used to dismiss certain compositions inferred through spectroscopy. This letter concludes by exploring applications of remote sensing in the quest for the search for life outside of our solar system.

As we advance into the next chapter in our search for life beyond Earth with state-of-the-art technology such as the James Webb Space Telescope, it is essential that we are able to accurately discern compositional information, including potential biosignatures, from exoplanet transmission spectra through atmospheric retrieval pipelines. As such, ensuring the efficacy of the models in these pipelines is more important than ever, and we face a major challenge in this pursuit: the parameterizations of aerosols such as clouds, dusts, and hazes. Aerosols are ubiquitous in the atmospheres of both Solar System bodies and exoplanets, and representing them accurately in exoplanet atmospheric models is key to deriving the best possible compositional information from transit spectra. Fortunately, we have the opportunity to use pre-existing Solar System observations to validate and improve exoplanet-focused approaches to representing aerosol structures. We derive aerosol profiles from occultation data of Solar System worlds with known atmospheric composition such as Mars. When compared to aerosol parameterizations in retrieval pipelines, these profiles provide an opportunity for ground-truth verification of exoplanet atmospheric characterization tools.

[8] Atmospheric Retrievals: Limitations, Challenges, and the Road Ahead

2026-06-00

Atmospheric retrieval is now the default framework for interpreting exoplanet and brown dwarf spectra from space and ground-based platforms, yet its limitations often become most apparent precisely in the high-quality data regime where it is most heavily applied. In this talk, I will focus on the challenges of contemporary retrieval approaches, drawing on examples across low- and high-resolution spectroscopy, multiple wavelength regimes, and substellar benchmark atmospheres. Key challenges include degeneracies between temperature structure, composition, and aerosols; biases introduced by incomplete or overly flexible model assumptions; the influence of priors in data-limited regimes; uncertainty in the "correctness" of the data and separating planetary signal from astrophysical noise sources; and the difficulty of validating inference when forward models are only approximate representations of complex, multidimensional atmospheres. I will then outline several future directions that can move the field forward. These include leveraging combined low-and-hi-res datasets, incorporating more realistic atmospheric physics without sacrificing interpretability, and inference methods that enable more rapid computation enabling more robustness tests. I will also briefly discuss the role of machine-learning techniques as computational accelerators and diagnostic tools, rather than black-box replacements for physical models. The goal is to provide a concise, critical perspective on how retrieval can evolve from a powerful but fragile technique into a robust framework for population-level studies and the eventual characterization of potentially habitable worlds.

[1] Impacts of Climate Variability on the Transmission Spectrum of TRAPPIST-1e

With the recent launch of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), terrestrial exoplanets will be at the forefront of exoplanetary research. Among those, habitable zone terrestrial exoplanets, particularly planets about M dwarfs such as TRAPPIST-1e, will be observed in a new capacity, as JWST's NIRSpec instrument will be able to perform high-precision infrared spectroscopic measurements of their atmospheres. TRAPPIST-1e has been previously well-studied as a potential habitable zone "ocean world," and is commonly used in atmospheric studies of habitable zone M dwarf exoplanets. Throughout its expected twenty year lifetime, JWST is expected to be able to detect strong CO<SUB>2</SUB>, CH<SUB>4</SUB>, and molecular oxygen signals during transit observations. The CO<SUB>2</SUB>-CH<SUB>4</SUB> pair in particular is expected to be a potential biosignature when seen at disequilibrium, which implies a potential biotic reaction. The characteristics of these spectra are dependent upon the atmospheric properties of the planet; cloud cover at higher altitudes can mask transmission signals from lower in the atmosphere and flatten the spectrum, while hotter temperatures and lower mean molecular weight increase the atmospheric scale height, which expands spectral features. Using the ExoCAM GCM and the Planetary Spectrum Generator (PSG), we run simulations for TRAPPIST-1e's known planetary parameters assuming an optimistic haze-free, tidally locked planet with an aquaplanet surface. We vary atmospheric compositions from 10<SUP>-4</SUP> bar to 1 bar of CO<SUB>2</SUB> in a 1 bar N<SUB>2</SUB> atmosphere, with modern Earth-like CH<SUB>4</SUB> mixing ratios. We investigate the relationship between NIRSpec detection significance of CO<SUB>2</SUB> and H<SUB>2</SUB>O and the climatology of TRAPPIST-1e's atmosphere, namely temperature and cloud top height. We demonstrate that in the optimistic haze-free case, H<SUB>2</SUB>O, CO<SUB>2</SUB>, and CH<SUB>4</SUB> would be detectable in a 10<SUP>-1</SUP> bar CO<SUB>2</SUB> atmosphere during JWST's lifespan, using transit spectra observations with NIRSpec/PRISM between 0.5 and 5 microns. We also explore the previously noted temporal variability in spectral feature strength, and its relationship with climatological variability in temperature and cloud cover. This broadly agrees with previous work, which found that H<SUB>2</SUB>O clouds would diminish, but not extinguish spectral features in the atmosphere of TRAPPIST-1e. Even in the pessimistic cloudy cases with hazes, JWST may still be able to constrain abundances of potential biosignature pairs such as CO<SUB>2</SUB>-CH<SUB>4</SUB> within its lifespan.

The excess absorption at 8.7 μm can be explained by the presence of small (∼0.01 μm) grains of SiO<SUB>2</SUB>[s] in the uppermost layers of HD 189733 b's dayside atmosphere. This is the first direct detection of silicate clouds in HD 189733 b's atmosphere, and the first detection of a distinct absorption feature from silicate clouds on the dayside of any hot Jupiter. We find that models including SiO<SUB>2</SUB>[s] are preferred by 6─7σ over clear models and those with other potential cloud species. The high-altitude location of these silicate particles is best explained by formation in the hottest regions of HD 189733 b's dayside atmosphere near the substellar point. We additionally find that HD 189733 b's emission spectrum longward of 9 μm displays residual features not well captured by our current atmospheric models. HD 189733b is the archetype of hot Jupiters. We propose to measure the molecular inventory and cloud composition in its atmosphere to high sensitivity. We will observe its transit spectrum over a large range of wavelength, using 5 transits: two observed with NIRCam grisms, and three with MIRI MRS. The resulting composite transit spectrum spans from 2.4 to beyond 20 microns, and includes strong bands of the major atmospheric molecules (water, methane, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxode), as well as strong bands of important minor species (HCN, ammonia, and hydrogen sulfide). There is evidence that exoplanets show a mass-metallicity trend that differs from planets in our Solar System when water vapor (oxygen) is used as the proxy for metallicity. We will measure the atmospheric metallicity of HD 189733b to a precision of 0.025-dex using CNO elements, and determine unequivocally whether it is consistent with the Solar System's relation, or not. We will also probe atmospheric chemical disequilibrium by detecting minor species that are depleted (methane) or enhanced by vertical transport (HCN), or produced by photochemistry (hydrogen sulfide, from sulfur photochemistry). Our analysis will successfully deal with possible interference due to stellar activity, and we will measure the cloud composition using vibrational modes in the thermal IR. Although this planet transits a very bright star (Kmag=5.54), we are using moderately high spectral resolution and the observations will not be hindered by saturation. These are low-risk observations for Cycle-1 because the signals to be measured are large, and the scientific return is substantial.

We present new ground-based optical transmission spectra of the hot Jupiter HD 189733b, derived from nine transits observed over a six year time span (2016-2021) using near-simultaneous $u^{\prime} g^{\prime} r^{\prime} i^{\prime} $ broadband observations. Our results indicate an enhanced spectral slope in the optical regime ≍2.4 times steeper than would be expected from canonical Rayleigh scattering and that is consistent with earlier measurements of a super-Rayleigh slope (SRS). While the effect of stellar activity on the transmission spectrum complicates the measurement of the spectral slope, our multiepoch data set over six years can measure and average over stellar variations, yielding a mean spectral index of -9.9 ± 4.4. The 1200 K equilibrium temperature of HD 189733b places it in a sweet spot for the formation of SRSs and is consistent with vigorously mixing hazes in the atmosphere. Additionally, we find variations in the depth of the lightcurve during two of the transits, explainable as an increase in occulted star spots during June 2021. Although the star is active, the mean level of stellar activity does not seem to vary dramatically over our six years of observations, leading us to conclude that the variability in stellar activity is modest at most.

[1] On the Effect of Stellar Activity on Low-resolution Transit Spectroscopy and the use of High Resolution as Mitigation

We present models designed to quantify the effects of stellar activity on exoplanet transit spectroscopy and atmospheric characterization at low (R = 100) and high (R = 100,000) spectral resolution. We study three model classes mirroring planetary system archetypes: a hot Jupiter around an early-K star (HD 189733 b); a mini-Neptune around an early-M dwarf (K2-18 b); and terrestrial planets around a late-M dwarf (TRAPPIST-1). We map photospheres with temperatures and radial velocities (RV) and integrate specific intensity stellar models. We obtain transit spectra affected by stellar contamination, the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect (RME), and center-to-limb variations (CLV). We find that, at low resolution, for later-type stars, planetary water features become difficult to distinguish from contamination. Many distributions of unocculted active regions can induce planetary-like features of similar amplitudes in the case of a late-M dwarf. Atmospheric characterization of planets around late-type stars will likely continue to suffer from degeneracy with stellar activity unless active regions' parameters can be constrained using additional information. For the early-K star, stellar contamination mostly manifests itself through a slope at optical wavelengths similar to Rayleigh scattering. In all cases, contamination induces offsets in measured planet radii. At high resolution, we show that we can determine the origin of H<SUB>2</SUB>O and CO detection signals and lift the degeneracy observed at low resolution, provided sufficient planet RV variation during transit and adequate correction for the RME and CLV when required. Context. The strength and location of these maxima vary depending on, for example, planet system parameters, instrumentation, and the number of removal iterations. We discuss why observers should therefore take several factors into account using a strategy akin to the `exposure triangle' employed in traditional photography where a balance must be struck by considering the full context of the observation. Our method is robust and may be employed by observers to estimate the best observational strategies for other targets.

When comparing atmospheric models to observations, it is common for multiple candidate models to produce a reasonable fit to the observed data. The variations in these models may be a result of different treatments of of atmospheric properties such as clouds and hazes, or different codes with small variations in their model implementation approaches. Typically, final conclusions are reached by selecting the best performing model according to some metric. However, this approach ignores model uncertainty in favour of specific assumptions made by the chosen model. We show that our ensemble methods lead to larger but more realistic uncertainties on retrieved parameters that account for inherent model uncertainty. We recommend stacking as the most robust method for combining retrieval results.

<BR /> Aims: We aim to investigate the origin of the discrepant results reported in the literature about the presence of Na I in the atmosphere of HD 209458 b, based on low- and high-resolution transmission spectroscopy. <BR /> Methods: We generated synthetic planetary atmosphere models and we compared them with the transmission light curves and spectra observed in previous studies. Either both datasets are interpreted as consistent with a total absence of Na I in the planetary atmosphere (with Hubble Space Telescope data being affected by limb darkening), or the terminator temperature of HD 209458 b has to have an upper limit of about 1000 K. In particular, we find that 1D transmission spectra with lower-than-equilibrium temperatures can also explain the previously reported detection of absorption signal at low resolution due to differential transit depth in adjacent bands, while the cores of the Na I D lines may be masked by the strong RM signal seen at high resolution. We also rule out high-altitude clouds, which would otherwise mask the absorption signal at low resolution, as the source of the discrepancies. <BR /> Conclusions: This work highlights the synergies between different observing techniques, specifically low- and high-resolution spectroscopy, to fully characterise transiting exoplanet systems.

Hot Jupiters present a major challenge to planet formation theories, and their atmospheric compositions are keys to understanding their origins. Despite extensive observations from both space and ground based facilities, the molecular makeup of keystone hot Jupiters - HD 209458 b and HD 189733 b has long been a topic of intense debate. More importantly, these two planets occupy the moderate hot Jupiter regime (1000 - 1500 K), cooler than the ultra-hot (T &gt; 2000 K) planets where molecules dissociate but hotter than warm Neptunes where condensation dominates, placing them in the critical temperature range where species such as H<SUB>2</SUB>O, CO, CH<SUB>4</SUB>, HCN, and NH<SUB>3</SUB> can coexist—ideal for probing chemical transitions between oxygen-rich and carbon-rich atmospheres. I will present our campaign to revisit these classic exoplanets using the simultaneous high-resolution H- and K-band coverage of IGRINS2. Our observations target the dayside thermal emission mitigating the biases plaguing transit geometry such as limb asymmetry, Rossiter-McLaughlin effects and clouds. I will present the preliminary result of a strong H<SUB>2</SUB>O and CO signals in HD209458b and an ongoing analysis of HD189733b with a strong H<SUB>2</SUB>O signal. Today, JWST is remarkable in detecting broadband exoplanet atmospheric features, but recovering crucial narrow band signals (e.g., CO) has proven to be challenging for planets with robust ground-based CO detection (e.g., WASP-18b, HD209458b). Our analysis of HD209458b and HD189733b further emphasizes the reasoning that ground-based observations are complementary to spaced-based facilities and possess unique advantages in providing unprecedented view of exoplanet atmospheres.

热木星对行星形成理论提出了重大挑战，其大气成分是理解其起源的关键。尽管来自空间和地面设施的观测非常丰富，关键热木星 HD 209458 b 和 HD 189733 b 的分子组成长期以来一直存在激烈争议。更重要的是，这两颗行星处于中等温度热木星区间（1000-1500 K），比分子解离主导的超热行星（T > 2000 K）更冷，但又比冷凝主导的温暖海王星更热，正处于 H2O、CO、CH4、HCN 和 NH3 等物种可以共存的关键温度区间——非常适合研究富氧与富碳大气之间的化学转变。我将介绍我们利用 IGRINS2 同步高分辨率 H- 和 K-波段观测重新研究这些经典系外行星的计划。我们的观测针对日面热发射，减小了凌星几何带来的偏差，如边缘不对称、Rossiter-McLaughlin 效应和云的影响。我将展示 HD209458b 中强 H2O 和 CO 信号的初步结果，以及 HD189733b 的持续分析（同样有强 H2O 信号）。目前，JWST 在探测宽带系外行星大气特征方面表现出色，但对于那些地面已稳健探测到 CO 的行星（如 WASP-18b、HD209458b），恢复关键的窄带信号（如 CO）仍然具有挑战性。我们对 HD209458b 和 HD189733b 的分析进一步强调，地面观测与空间设施互为补充，并在提供前所未有的系外行星大气视角方面具有独特优势。

[1] Adapting ExoMol line lists for high-resolution studies: methane as an example

2024-07-00

The ExoMol database (Tennyson+ 2020 J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transf., 225, 107228) provides extensive line lists and key molecular properties applicable across a broad of temperatures: including energy levels, and transitions, opacities, lifetimes, partition functions, and other relevant information. The database is widely used to interpret spectra from JWST (James Webb Space Telescope) and elsewhere. <P />The ExoMol methodology relies on the quantum mechanical treatment of the problem for each molecule with electronic motion represented by potential energy and dipole moment surfaces which provide inputs for nuclear motion programs (DUO, TROVE, DVR3D, EVEREST), enabling the generation of line lists. These line lists are designed to model molecular spectra over a wide range of temperatures for both parent and isotopically-substituted molecules. ExoMol data is being widely used to interpret JWST observations, for example leading to the detection of sulfur dioxide in exoplanet WASP-39b (Alderson+ 2023 Nature, 664, 6994) and ammonia in cool brown dwarf WISEJ1828 (Barrado+ 2023 Nature, 624, 263). The current database contains line lists and opacities for approximately a hundred molecules (250+ isotopologues), see data release ExoMol 2024 (Tennyson+ 2024 J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transf., submitted). <P />The ExoMolHD (ExoMol in High Definition) project delivers accurate molecular line lists tailored for the studies of exoplanetary atmospheres in the current era of high-resolution (R=100000) observations. ExoMolHD combines this theoretical approach with extensive sets of accurate experimental data to enhance the applicability of these line lists for high-resolution studies. <P />A key molecule is methane, CH_4. Methane plays a vital role in astrochemistry. It is one of the dominant constituents of the atmospheres of brown dwarfs, it has been detected in hot atmospheres of exoplanets and is considered a biosignature on terrestrial planets. The ExoMol methodology was used to produce a complete and accurate line list for methane, the recent Exomol MM (MARVELous Methane) line list (Yurchenko+ 2024 Mon. Not. Roy. Astron. Soc., 528, 3719). In particular, over 50 billion transitions were calculated with the variational program TROVE (Theoretical ROVibrational Energies) and subsequently improved by incorporating empirical energy levels computed with the MARVEL (Measured Active Rotational-Vibrational Energy Levels) algorithm of Furtenbacher+ (2007 J. Molec. Spectrosc., 245, 115) from assigned measured transitions and associated uncertainties collected from the literature (Kefala+ 2024 J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transf., 316, 108897). More than 80000 experimental transitions were collected from 96 sources to derive over 23000 energy levels with full assignments and uncertainties. Finally, over 1 million line positions with experimental accuracy were derived from this procedure. <P />The ExoMol/ExoMolHD are (a) expanding our representation of the effects of pressure on molecular spectra using a mixture of full quantum mechanical treatments, semi-empirical models and machine learning; (b) constructing line lists for important isotopically substituted molecules (McKemmish+ 2024 RAS Tech. Instr., in preparation), (c) extending calculations into the ultraviolet with a particular focus on modeling the temperature-dependence of photodissociation as photochemistry provides a key driver of atmospheric processes in many exoplanets.

[1] 为高分辨率研究适配ExoMol谱线表：以甲烷为例

ExoMol 数据库（Tennyson+ 2020 J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transf., 225, 107228）提供了适用于广泛温度范围的详尽谱线表和关键分子性质，包括能级、跃迁、消光系数、寿命、配分函数及其他相关信息。该数据库被广泛用于解释 JWST（James Webb Space Telescope）及其他观测设备获得的光谱。<P />ExoMol 方法依赖于对每个分子的量子力学处理，电子运动通过势能面和偶极矩面表示，为核运动程序（DUO、TROVE、DVR3D、EVEREST）提供输入，从而生成谱线表。这些谱线表旨在模拟母体分子及其同位素取代分子的分子光谱，覆盖广泛温度范围。ExoMol 数据被广泛用于解释 JWST 观测，例如促成了系外行星 WASP-39b 中二氧化硫的探测（Alderson+ 2023 Nature, 664, 6994）以及冷褐矮星 WISEJ1828 中氨的探测（Barrado+ 2023 Nature, 624, 263）。当前数据库包含约一百种分子（250+ 同位素体）的谱线表和消光系数，详见数据发布 ExoMol 2024（Tennyson+ 2024 J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transf., submitted）。<P />ExoMolHD（ExoMol in High Definition）项目为当前高分辨率（R=100000）观测时代的系外行星大气研究提供了高精度分子谱线表。ExoMolHD 将理论方法与大量高精度实验数据结合，提升了这些谱线表在高分辨率研究中的适用性。<P />甲烷（CH_4）是关键分子。甲烷在天体化学中起着重要作用，是褐矮星大气的主要成分之一，已在系外行星的高温大气中被探测到，并被认为是类地行星上的生物标志物。ExoMol 方法用于生成了完整且精确的甲烷谱线表，即最新的 Exomol MM（MARVELous Methane）谱线表（Yurchenko+ 2024 Mon. Not. Roy. Astron. Soc., 528, 3719）。具体来说，使用变分程序 TROVE（Theoretical ROVibrational Energies）计算了超过 500 亿个跃迁，并通过结合 MARVEL（Measured Active Rotational-Vibrational Energy Levels）算法（Furtenbacher+ 2007 J. Molec. Spectrosc., 245, 115）从文献收集的已分配测量跃迁及其相关不确定性，进一步提升了能级的精度（Kefala+ 2024 J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transf., 316, 108897）。共收集了来自 96 个来源的 80000 多个实验跃迁，用于推导 23000 多个能级，均有完整分配和不确定性。最终，通过该流程获得了超过 100 万条具有实验精度的谱线位置。<P />ExoMol/ExoMolHD 正在（a）通过全量子力学处理、半经验模型和机器学习相结合，扩展我们对压力对分子光谱影响的描述；（b）为重要的同位素取代分子构建谱线表（McKemmish+ 2024 RAS Tech. Instr., in preparation）；（c）将计算扩展到紫外波段，特别关注光解作用的温度依赖性建模，因为光化学过程是许多系外行星大气过程的关键驱动力。

[2] Line Lists for High Resolution Studies of Exoplanets

2021-06-00

The ExoMol project (www.exomol.com) provides comprehensive line lists for the study of exoplanets and other hot bodies. As part of the ERC-funded ExoMolHD project these line lists are being refactored to facilitate their use in characterization of exoplanets using high resolution Doppler shift spectroscopy. This technique is based the use of MARVEL (measured active rotation vibration energy level) to obtain empirical energy levels and illustrated by a recent study on formaldhyde (H$_2$CO). For formaldehyde we analysed of 16 596 non-redundant transitions from 43 experimental sources and resulted in the determination of 5029 empirical energy levels. As part of this work new measurements were performed in Bologna yielding high-accuracy rotational transitions within the ground, \nub{3}, \nub{4} and \nub{6} vibrational states, significantly improving the overall accuracy of the network. Eleven artificial transitions determined from effective Hamiltonian fits were added to the network to both fix the gap between ortho and para levels, and to join free-standing networks of transitions to the main network. The empirical energies were used to update the AYTY ExoMol line list for formaldehyde. This yielded 367 779 transition frequencies determined using the empirical energy levels of which 183 673 lie above the dynamic HITRAN intensity cutoff. The generation of line lists which combine empirically-determined transition wavenumbers with {\it ab initio} transition dipoles is suitable for high resolution studies of both the Earth's and exoplanetary atmospheres. High resoltion line lists for other molecules starting with AlO, VO and the isotopologues of H$_3^+$ are currently being prepared. <P />A. R. {Al-Derzi}, S. N. Yurchenko, J. Tennyson, M. Melosso, Ningjing Jiang, C. Puzzarini, L. Dore, T. Furtenbacher, R. Tobias and A G. Császár, 2021, J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transf., doi = {10.1016/j.jqsrt.2021.107563

[2] 用于系外行星高分辨率研究的谱线列表

ExoMol项目（www.exomol.com）为系外行星及其他高温天体的研究提供了全面的谱线表。作为ERC资助的ExoMolHD项目的一部分，这些谱线表正在重构，以便于利用高分辨率多普勒位移光谱对系外行星进行特性刻画。这一技术基于MARVEL（实测主动转动-振动能级）获得经验能级，并以最近对甲醛（H$_2$CO）的研究为例。对于甲醛，我们分析了来自43个实验来源的16,596个非冗余跃迁，确定了5029个经验能级。作为该工作的一部分，在博洛尼亚进行了新测量，获得了基态、\nub{3}、\nub{4}和\nub{6}振动态内的高精度转动跃迁，显著提升了整体网络的准确性。通过有效哈密顿量拟合确定的11个人工跃迁被加入网络，用于弥合ortho和para能级之间的间隙，并将独立的跃迁网络连接到主网络。经验能级被用于更新甲醛的AYTY ExoMol谱线表。由此得到的367,779个跃迁频率是基于经验能级确定的，其中183,673个高于HITRAN动态强度阈值。结合经验跃迁波数和从头算跃迁偶极矩生成的谱线表，适用于地球和系外行星大气的高分辨率研究。其他分子的高分辨率谱线表（如AlO、VO及H$_3^+$的同位素体）目前正在编制中。<P />A. R. {Al-Derzi}, S. N. Yurchenko, J. Tennyson, M. Melosso, Ningjing Jiang, C. Puzzarini, L. Dore, T. Furtenbacher, R. Tobias 和 A G. Császár, 2021, J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. [3] Influence of molecular collisions on the atmospheric modelling: new data and updates in spectroscopic databases

2024-09-00

The advent of new-generation space missions (such as WFIRST and ARIEL) as well as high-performance observatories both space-born and ground-based (such as JWST and ELTs) should start to answer fundamental questions about the formation, composition and properties of exoplanets. A reliable interpretation of the observations will rely on a huge amount of spectroscopic data, with a particular emphasis on high-resolution spectroscopic data.Because of the extreme conditions characteristic of exoplanetary atmospheres (high temperatures and high levels of insolation), much information on molecular processes and their spectroscopic signatures is not available. In particular, lack of adequate procedures to measure or calculate collisional line-shape parameters for billions of transitions required limits severely the quality of the atmospheric modelling and retrievals. Line-shape profiles and pressure-broadening coefficients for "exotic" molecular species constitute a basis for cross-sections calculations which are further used to calculate atmospheric opacities. It was shown recently [1] that account of pressure-broadening effect on the spectral line shapes is essential to enhance our capacity for studying exoplanets. Several spectroscopic databases, such as HITRAN [2], GEISA [3], ExoMol [4], TheoReTS [5] and MoLList [6]) provide extensive line lists of positions and intensities of isolated spectral transitions, some of which contain many billions of lines. However, the associated pressure-broadening and shift parameters, as well as their temperature dependences, remain poorly determined or completely missing. Therefore, there is a huge demand for robust theoretical approaches and estimates that could provide line-shape parameters for a large range of excitations covering wide ranges of temperatures and pressures and large variety of perturbers.First steps in this direction have been made recently with developing at least approximate theoretical approaches [7] to getting pressure-broadening parameters for most infrared-active molecules detected or expected in exoplanetary atmospheres. Rotationally independent estimates of pressure-broadening coefficients have been generated for more than 50 active species (see Table) and 12 perturbers (Ar, CH4, CO, CO2, H2, H2O, He, N2, NH3, NO, O2 and self). Full data sets have been put in a specifically designed for this purpose prototype database COLLINE [8] for testing, and one-value data have been selected for each molecular pair for including in the 2024 release [4] of ExoMol.Table: Exomolecules with new line-broadening coefficients. AlCl AlH AlO AsH3 BeH C3 CaF CaH CaO CaOH CH2 CH3 CP CrH CS FeO KCl KF KOH LiCl LiF LiH LiH+ MgF MgH MgO NaCl NaF NaH NaOH NH NS PF3 PH PN PO PO2 PS ScH SH SH3 SiC SiH SiH2 SiH3 SiO SiO2 SiS TiF TiH TiO VO In this work, we describe the main features of newly produced line-broadening data, their organization in the COLLINE database and selection of some of them for including in ExoMol. We provide also some examples showing the influence of different pertubers on the cross-sections calculated for active molecules. Ways to further populating of databases for exoplanetary molecules will be outlined. References[1] J.J. Fortney, T.D. Robinson, S. Domagal-Goldman et al., arXiv:1905.07064 (2019)[2] I.E. Gordon, L.S. [3] 分子碰撞对大气建模的影响：光谱数据库中的新数据与更新

新一代空间任务（如WFIRST和ARIEL）以及高性能的空间和地面天文台（如JWST和ELTs）的出现，将开始解答有关系外行星形成、组成和性质的基本问题。对观测结果的可靠解释依赖于大量光谱数据，尤其是高分辨率光谱数据。由于系外行星大气的极端条件（高温和高照射），关于分子过程及其光谱特征的信息严重不足。特别是，缺乏适当的程序来测量或计算数十亿跃迁所需的碰撞线型参数，严重限制了大气建模和检索的质量。线型轮廓和压强展宽系数对于“非常规”分子物种来说，是计算截面进而计算大气不透明度的基础。最近的研究[1]表明，考虑压强展宽对光谱线型的影响对于提升我们研究系外行星的能力至关重要。多个光谱数据库，如HITRAN[2]、GEISA[3]、ExoMol[4]、TheoReTS[5]和MoLList[6]，提供了大量孤立光谱跃迁的位置和强度线表，其中一些包含数十亿条谱线。然而，相关的压强展宽和位移参数及其温度依赖性仍然测定不足或完全缺失。因此，迫切需要稳健的理论方法和估算，能够为广泛激发态、宽温压范围和多种扰动体提供线型参数。最近在这一方向上已取得初步进展，开发了至少近似的理论方法[7]，用于获得大多数在系外行星大气中已探测或预期的红外活性分子的压强展宽参数。已为50多种活性物种（见表）和12种扰动体（Ar, CH4, CO, CO2, H2, H2O, He, N2, NH3, NO, O2及自展宽）生成了与转动无关的压强展宽系数估算。完整数据集已被放入专为此目的设计的原型数据库COLLINE[8]进行测试，并为每对分子选择了一个数值用于2024年ExoMol[4]发布。表：具有新展宽系数的系外分子。AlCl AlH AlO AsH3 BeH C3 CaF CaH CaO CaOH CH2 CH3 CP CrH CS FeO KCl KF KOH LiCl LiF LiH LiH+ MgF MgH MgO NaCl NaF NaH NaOH NH NS PF3 PH PN PO PO2 PS ScH SH SH3 SiC SiH SiH2 SiH3 SiO SiO2 SiS TiF TiH TiO VO 本文描述了新生成的线展宽数据的主要特征、其在COLLINE数据库中的组织方式，以及部分数据被选入ExoMol的过程。我们还提供了一些例子，展示不同扰动体对活性分子计算截面的影响。最后将概述进一步扩充系外行星分子数据库的方法。参考文献[1] J.J. [4] Provision of high-definition pressure-broadening data for spectroscopic studies of exoplanetary atmospheres: ExoMol Diet 1.2

2022-09-00

Spectroscopic studies of exoplanetary atmospheres by the next generation space missions, such as the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and Atmospheric Remote-sensing Exoplanet Large-survey (ARIEL), will rely on spectroscopic data available at mid-infrared and visible/infrared wavelengths for the bulk of already detected or expected molecules. While in gas giants the main perturbers are hydrogen (H2) and helium (He), due to the large variety of exoplanet atmospheres to be probed, a whole range of other broadeners are also of interest, including carbon dioxide (CO2), nitrogen (N2), oxygen (O2), water vapor (H2O), carbon monoxide (CO), nitric monoxide (NO), methane (CH4) and ammonia (NH3). Moreover, because of the elevated temperatures encountered, not only "exotic" molecules but also molecular ions have to be considered as optically active species.Several spectroscopic databases (e.g., HITRAN [1], GEISA [2], ExoMol [3], TheoReTS [4] and MoLList [5]) provide extensive line lists of positions and intensities of isolated spectral transitions, some of which contain many billions of lines. However, the associated pressure-broadening and shift parameters, as well as their temperature dependences, remain poorly determined or completely missing (see Figure). In addition, due to the specific conditions of hot atmospheres and chemical reactions which lead to the formation of spectroscopically active species, laboratory studies are extremely scarce in both infrared/microwave (IR/MW) and visible/ultraviolet(UV) regions. Therefore, there is a huge demand for robust theoretical approaches and estimates that could provide line-shape parameters for a large range of excitations covering wide ranges of temperatures and pressures and large variety of perturbers.Figure: Availability of line broadening parameters in spectroscopic databases: missing (white), limited coverage (light green) and good coverage (dark green). In this work, we introduce recipes for getting reasonable estimates of pressure line-broadening parameters and their temperature dependences for IR/MW (vibrotational) and UV (vibronic) transitions for molecules relevant to exoplanetary atmospheres including "exotic" neutral and ionic species (such as NO+, HCO+, H3O+, HeH+ and H3+, NH4+).The existing classical, quantum-mechanical and semi-classical theoretical approaches to collisional line-broadening and shifting used for the IR/MW region require pre-computed reliable potential-energy surfaces and CPU-costly calculations for each collisional pair. Here we suggest a simple theoretical expression requiring a minimal set of input parameters (kinetic molecular properties and the character of the leading term in the intermolecular interaction potential) [6]. Good consistency with available measurements over the temperature range 200-3000 K is demonstrated for NO and OH colliding with rare-gas atoms and non-polar molecules. Not only active neutral molecules but also molecular ions such as NO+, HCO+, H3O+, HeH+ (which have permanent dipole moments) and H3+, NH4+ (with only transition dipole moments) can be treated by this approach.In addition to the recipe for getting estimates, for the IR/MW region we consider traditional semiclassical calculation methods combined with accurate variational wavefunctions for large-scale calculations: a new program for computing line widths and shifts, based on the use of ExoMol ro-vibrational wavefunctions to compute the key (reduced) matrix elements. Given the large number of molecules, transitions, broadeners and range of temperatures required, we also explore the use of machine learng methods trained on data for selected systems to compute comprehensive and very large rotation-vibration and rovibronic pressure-broadening parameters.For the UV region, where the lack of the line-shape data is especially critical, more accurate models, motivated by the known effect of the strongly dominating adiabatic collisions and based on the Fourier-integral/phase-shift theory, are introduced to take account of real molecular trajectories and very different interaction potentials of the active molecule in the initial and final states. Examples of applications for line lists from the ExoMol database are given.The theoretical models presented will be incorporated into an updated ExoMol diet [7] to provide default line-broadening parameters when none are available from other sources and will be used to develop stand-alone approaches for automatic, large-scale production of collisional widths/shifts for line lists containing billions of transitions for molecules of interest for atmospheres of exoplanets. [4] 为系外行星大气光谱研究提供高分辨率压力展宽数据：ExoMol Diet 1.2

下一代空间任务（如James Webb Space Telescope（JWST）和Atmospheric Remote-sensing Exoplanet Large-survey（ARIEL））对系外行星大气的光谱学研究，将依赖于中红外和可见/红外波段已探测或预期分子的光谱数据。对于气态巨行星，主要的展宽体是氢（H2）和氦（He），但由于未来要探测的系外行星大气类型多样，其他展宽体也很重要，包括二氧化碳（CO2）、氮气（N2）、氧气（O2）、水蒸气（H2O）、一氧化碳（CO）、一氧化氮（NO）、甲烷（CH4）和氨（NH3）。此外，由于高温环境，不仅“非常规”分子，还需考虑分子离子作为光学活性物种。多个光谱数据库（如HITRAN [1]、GEISA [2]、ExoMol [3]、TheoReTS [4]和MoLList [5]）提供了大量孤立光谱跃迁的线位置和强度表，其中部分数据库包含数十亿条谱线。然而，相关的压强展宽和频移参数及其温度依赖性仍然测定不足或完全缺失（见图）。此外，由于高温大气的特殊条件和化学反应导致的光谱活性物种形成，实验室在红外/微波（IR/MW）和可见/紫外（UV）波段的研究极为稀缺。因此，亟需稳健的理论方法和估算，能够为广泛的激发态、温度、压强和展宽体提供线型参数。图：光谱数据库中线展宽参数的可用性：缺失（白色）、覆盖有限（浅绿色）、覆盖良好（深绿色）。本工作介绍了为系外行星大气相关分子（包括“非常规”中性和离子物种，如NO+、HCO+、H3O+、HeH+和H3+、NH4+）的IR/MW（振转）和UV（电子振动）跃迁获得合理压强展宽参数及其温度依赖性的估算方法。现有的经典、量子力学和半经典理论方法用于IR/MW区的碰撞展宽和频移，需要预先计算可靠的势能面，并对每一对碰撞体进行高计算量的计算。我们提出了一种简单的理论表达式，仅需最少的输入参数（分子的动力学性质和分子间相互作用势的主导项特性）[6]。该方法在200-3000 K温度范围内，对NO和OH与稀有气体原子及非极性分子的碰撞展现出与实验数据良好的一致性。不仅适用于活性中性分子，也适用于如NO+、HCO+、H3O+、HeH+（具有永久偶极矩）和H3+、NH4+（仅有跃迁偶极矩）等分子离子。此外，针对IR/MW区，我们还考虑了结合精确变分波函数的传统半经典计算方法，用于大规模计算：开发了基于ExoMol转动-振动波函数计算关键（约化）矩阵元的新程序，用于计算谱线宽度和频移。鉴于所需分子、跃迁、展宽体和温度范围极其庞大，我们还探索了利用针对特定体系训练的数据的机器学习方法，来计算全面且极大的转动-振动和转动-电子振动压强展宽参数。对于UV区，因线型数据极度缺乏，我们引入了更精确的模型，这些模型基于已知的绝热碰撞主导效应和傅里叶积分/相移理论，能够考虑分子在初末态下真实的运动轨迹和截然不同的相互作用势。给出了ExoMol数据库线表的应用实例。所提出的理论模型将被整合进更新版ExoMol diet [7]，为其他来源无法提供参数时提供默认线展宽参数，并用于开发独立方法，实现对包含数十亿跃迁的线表自动大规模生成碰撞展宽/频移参数，这些分子对系外行星大气研究具有重要意义。参考文献：[1] I.E. [5] Computational Infrared Spectroscopy of 956 Phosphorus-bearing Molecules

2021-04-00

Phosphine is now well established as a biosignature, which has risen to prominence with its recent tentative detection on Venus. To follow up this discovery and related future exoplanet biosignature detections, it is important to spectroscopically detect the presence of phosphorus-bearing atmospheric molecules that could be involved in the chemical networks producing, destroying or reacting with phosphine. We start by enumerating phosphorus-bearing molecules (P-molecules) that could potentially be detected spectroscopically in planetary atmospheres and collecting all available spectral data. Gaseous P-molecules are rare, with speciation information scarce. Very few molecules have high accuracy spectral data from experiment or theory; instead, the best current spectral data was obtained using a high-throughput computational algorithm, RASCALL, relying on functional group theory to efficiently produce approximate spectral data for arbitrary molecules based on their component functional groups. Here, we present a high-throughput approach utilising established computational quantum chemistry methods (CQC) to produce a database of approximate infrared spectra for 958 P-molecules. These data are of interest for astronomy and astrochemistry (importantly identifying potential ambiguities in molecular assignments), improving RASCALL's underlying data, big data spectral analysis and future machine learning applications. However, this data will probably not be sufficiently accurate for secure experimental detections of specific molecules within complex gaseous mixtures in laboratory or astronomy settings. We chose the strongly performing harmonic $\omega$B97X-D/def2-SVPD model chemistry for all molecules and use the more sophisticated and time-consuming GVPT2 anharmonic model chemistry for 250 smaller molecules. Limitations to our automated approach, particularly for the less robust GVPT2 method, are considered along with pathways to future improvements. Our CQC calculations significantly improve on existing RASCALL data by providing quantitative intensities, new data in the fingerprint region (crucial for molecular identification) and higher frequency regions (overtones, combination bands), and improved data for fundamental transitions based on the specific chemical environment. As the spectroscopy of most P-molecules has never studied outside RASCALL and this approach, the new data in this paper is the most accurate spectral data available for most P-molecules and represent a significant advance in the understanding of the spectroscopic behaviour of these molecules.

[5] 956 种含磷分子的计算红外光谱

磷化氢现已被公认为生物标志物，因其近期在金星上的初步探测而备受关注。为跟进这一发现及未来相关系外行星生物标志物的探测，重要的是通过光谱学探测可能参与磷化氢生成、破坏或反应的含磷大气分子。我们首先列举了可能在行星大气中通过光谱学探测到的含磷分子（P-分子），并收集了所有可用的光谱数据。气态P-分子稀少，物种信息有限。极少数分子拥有实验或理论获得的高精度光谱数据；目前最好的光谱数据主要通过高通量计算算法RASCALL获得，该算法依赖官能团理论，基于组分官能团高效生成任意分子的近似光谱数据。本文提出了一种利用成熟计算量子化学方法（CQC）的高通量方法，生成了958种P-分子的近似红外光谱数据库。这些数据对天文学和天体化学具有重要意义（尤其有助于识别分子归属中的潜在歧义），可用于改进RASCALL基础数据、大数据光谱分析及未来机器学习应用。然而，这些数据可能尚不足以在实验室或天文环境中对复杂气体混合物中特定分子实现可靠实验探测。我们为所有分子选择了表现优异的谐振$\omega$B97X-D/def2-SVPD模型化学，并对250种较小分子采用了更复杂且耗时的GVPT2非谐模型化学。我们讨论了自动化方法的局限性，特别是GVPT2方法的稳健性问题，并提出了未来改进路径。我们的CQC计算通过提供定量强度、指纹区（对分子识别至关重要）及高频区（泛音、组合带）新数据，以及基于具体化学环境的基频跃迁改进数据，显著提升了现有RASCALL数据。由于大多数P-分子的光谱学研究仅限于RASCALL及本方法，本文新数据是目前大多数P-分子的最精确光谱数据，代表了对这些分子光谱行为理解的重要进步。

[6] The 2024 release of the ExoMol database: Molecular line lists for exoplanet and other hot atmospheres

2024-11-00

The ExoMol database (www.exomol.com) provides molecular data for spectroscopic studies of hot atmospheres. These data are widely used to model atmospheres of exoplanets, cool stars and other astronomical objects, as well as a variety of terrestrial applications. The 2024 data release reports the current status of the database which contains recommended line lists for 91 molecules and 224 isotopologues giving a total of almost 10<SUP>12</SUP> individual transitions. New features of the database include extensive "MARVELization" of line lists to allow them to be used for high resolutions studies, extension of several line lists to ultraviolet wavelengths, provision of photodissociation cross-sections and extended provision of broadening parameters. Some of the in-house data specifications have been rewritten in JSON and moved for conformity with other international standards. Data products, including specific heats, a database of lifetimes for plasma studies, and the ExoMolHR web app which allows exclusively high resolution data to be extracted, are discussed.

[6] 2024年ExoMol数据库发布：用于系外行星及其他高温大气的分子谱线表

ExoMol数据库（www.exomol.com）为高温大气的光谱学研究提供分子数据。这些数据被广泛用于系外行星、冷星及其他天体的大气建模，以及多种地面应用。2024年数据发布报告了数据库的最新状态，目前包含91种分子和224种同位素体的推荐谱线表，总计近10^12条单独跃迁。数据库的新特性包括对谱线表进行大规模“MARVEL化”，以支持高分辨率研究，扩展了若干谱线表至紫外波段，提供了光解截面和更广泛的展宽参数。部分内部数据规范已用JSON重写，并与其他国际标准接轨。数据产品还包括定压热容、用于等离子体研究的寿命数据库，以及ExoMolHR网页应用（可专门提取高分辨率数据）等内容。

2026-01-00

OH radical can be found in comets, stellar atmospheres, planetary atmospheres, interstellar clouds, exoplanets, the solar photosphere, and sunspots, making it a significant astrophysical molecule. Its detection relies on its emission properties, intrinsic to the molecules' rovibrational levels. This work presents high-level ab initio calculations of the electronic structure of OH radical using complete active space self consistent field/multiReference configuration interaction calculations, including Davidson correction methods with large basis sets and extensive treatment of the electron correlation. The adiabatic potential energy curves of the low-lying doublet and quartet electronic states of the hydroxyl, in the representation <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:msup><mml:mrow></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn><mml:mi>S</mml:mi><mml:mo>+</mml:mo><mml:mn>1</mml:mn></mml:mrow></mml:msup><mml:msup><mml:mrow><mml:mi>Λ</mml:mi></mml:mrow><mml:mrow><mml:mo>(</mml:mo><mml:mrow><mml:mo>+</mml:mo><mml:mo>/</mml:mo><mml:mo>−</mml:mo></mml:mrow><mml:mo>)</mml:mo></mml:mrow></mml:msup></mml:mrow></mml:math></inline-formula>, are investigated. Additionally, a systematic investigation of the transition dipole moment function (TDMF) for the <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>B</mml:mi><mml:mmultiscripts><mml:mi>Σ</mml:mi><mml:mo>+</mml:mo><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mmultiscripts><mml:mo>−</mml:mo><mml:mi>X</mml:mi><mml:mmultiscripts><mml:mi>Π</mml:mi><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mmultiscripts></mml:mrow></mml:math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>D</mml:mi><mml:mmultiscripts><mml:mi>Σ</mml:mi><mml:mo>−</mml:mo><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mmultiscripts><mml:mo>−</mml:mo><mml:mi>X</mml:mi><mml:mmultiscripts><mml:mi>Π</mml:mi><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mmultiscripts></mml:mrow></mml:math></inline-formula> transitions has been done along with the Franck-Condon factors of these systems. The computed TDMF and potential energy function are used in Le Roy's LEVEL and Western's PGOPHER programs, in combination with experimental literature line positions, to calculate rovibronic <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>B</mml:mi><mml:mmultiscripts><mml:mi>Σ</mml:mi><mml:mo>+</mml:mo><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mmultiscripts><mml:mo>−</mml:mo><mml:mi>X</mml:mi><mml:mmultiscripts><mml:mi>Π</mml:mi><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mmultiscripts></mml:mrow></mml:math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>D</mml:mi><mml:mmultiscripts><mml:mi>Σ</mml:mi><mml:mo>−</mml:mo><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mmultiscripts><mml:mo>−</mml:mo><mml:mi>X</mml:mi><mml:mmultiscripts><mml:mi>Π</mml:mi><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:mmultiscripts></mml:mrow></mml:math></inline-formula> transitions. The corresponding "first principles"-based line lists include line intensities, line positions with the relevant quantum numbers of the upper and lower states, e/f parity, and Einstein <inline-formula><mml:math><mml:mrow><mml:mi>A</mml:mi></mml:mrow></mml:math></inline-formula> coefficients. The results show good agreement with previously published experimental and theoretical data, including a corresponding updated MARVEL (measured active rotational-vibrational energy levels) analysis of the lowest excited states of the OH molecule.

[7] OH自由基的第一性原理研究：BΣ+2−XΠ2和DΣ−2−XΠ2转动-振动-电子跃迁

OH自由基可在彗星、恒星大气、行星大气、星际云、系外行星、太阳光球层和太阳黑子中发现，是重要的天体物理分子。其探测依赖于分子本身的转动-振动能级的发射特性。本工作采用高水平从头算方法，对OH自由基的电子结构进行了完全活性空间自洽场/多参考组态相互作用（CASSCF/MRCI）计算，结合Davidson修正方法、大基组和广泛的电子相关处理。研究了羟基低能双重态和四重态的绝热势能曲线（2S+1Λ(+/−)表示）。此外，系统考察了B2Σ+−X2Π和D2Σ−−X2Π跃迁的跃迁偶极矩函数（TDMF），并计算了这些体系的Franck-Condon因子。所计算的TDMF和势能函数结合实验文献中的谱线位置，利用Le Roy的LEVEL和Western的PGOPHER程序，计算了B2Σ+−X2Π和D2Σ−−X2Π的转动-振动-电子跃迁。所得“第一性原理”谱线表包括谱线强度、谱线位置、上下能级的相关量子数、e/f宇称和Einstein A系数。结果与先前发表的实验和理论数据良好一致，并包括对OH分子最低激发态的最新MARVEL（实测有效转动-振动能级）分析。

2022-01-00

Context. Collecting a large variety of exoplanetary atmosphere measurements is crucial to improve our understanding of exoplanets. In this context, it is likely that the field would benefit from broad species surveys, particularly using transit spectroscopy, which is the most successful technique of exoplanetary atmosphere characterization so far. <BR /> Aims: Our goal is to develop a model-unbiased technique using transit spectroscopy to analyze every qualified atomic spectral line in exoplanetary transit data, and search for relative absorption, that is, a decrease in the flux of the line when the planet is transiting. <BR /> Methods: We analyzed archive data from HDS at Subaru, HIRES at Keck, UVES at VLT, and HARPS at LaSilla to test our spectral survey methodology. It first filtered individual lines by relative noise levels. It also corrected for spectral offsets and telluric contamination. Our methodology performed an analysis along time and wavelength. The latter employed a bootstrap corroboration. <BR /> Results: We highlight the possible detections of Mn I and V II in HD 209459b data taken by HDS at Subaru (5.9σ at 5916.4 Å, 5.1σ at 6021.8 Å). The previous detection of Ca I in the same planet is classified as inconclusive by our algorithm, but we support the previous detection of Sc II (3.5σ at 6604.6 Å). We also highlight the possible detection of Ca I, Sc II, and Ti II in HD 189733 data taken by UVES at VLT (4.4σ at 6572.8 Å, 6.8σ at 6604.6 Å, and 3.5σ at 5910.1 Å), in addition to the possible detection of Al I in WASP-74b data taken by UVES at VLT (5.6σ at 6696.0 Å).

[1] Exploring the habitability and observability of Proxima b with ANDES and PCS

2026-04-00

Upcoming ELT instruments such as ANDES and PCS will soon enable atmospheric characterization of nearby non-transiting terrestrial exoplanets around M dwarf stars that were previously not accessible thanks to a new method combining high-contrast imaging and high-resolution spectroscopy in reflected light. A "golden sample" of five temperate rocky exoplanets was identified and will be observed with ANDES. In this study, we will focus on one of these targets: Proxima Centauri b. Previous studies performed climate simulations of Proxima b to explore its habitability. They showed that a broad range of atmospheric compositions allows the planet to sustain liquid water on its surface, suggesting that the planet could be habitable. In this study, we aim to re-explore the possible climate regimes of Proxima b using a fast new ocean model coupled to the Generic Planetary Climate Model (GPCM, Forget et al. in prep), which is a compromise between the simple version of the static ocean model used in Turbet et al. (2016) and a full 3D dynamic ocean model as in Del Genio et al. (2019). Additionally, to prepare upcoming observations, we aim to study the detectability of the planet to be able to efficiently characterize its atmosphere. [1] On the Dayside Atmosphere of WASP-12b

2022-06-00

The atmospheric structure of WASP-12b has been hotly contested for years, with disagreements on the presence of a thermal inversion as well as the carbon-to-oxygen ratio, C/O, due to retrieved abundances of H<SUB>2</SUB>O, CO<SUB>2</SUB>, and other included species such as HCN and C<SUB>2</SUB>H<SUB>2</SUB>. Previously, these difficult-to-diagnose discrepancies have been attributed to model differences; assumptions in these models were thought to drive retrievals toward different answers. Here, we show that some of these differences are independent of model assumptions and are instead due to subtle differences in the inputs, such as the eclipse depths and line-list databases. We replicate previously published retrievals and find that the retrieved results are data driven and are mostly unaffected by the addition of species such as HCN and C<SUB>2</SUB>H<SUB>2</SUB>. We also propose a new physically motivated model that takes into consideration the formation of H<SUP>-</SUP> via the thermal dissociation of H<SUB>2</SUB>O and H<SUB>2</SUB> at the temperatures reached in the dayside atmosphere of WASP-12b, but the data's current resolution does not support its inclusion in the atmospheric model. This study raises the concern that other exoplanet retrievals may be similarly sensitive to slight changes in the input data.

[3] Parameter degeneracies associated with interpreting HST WFC3 transmission spectra of exoplanetary atmospheres

2025-04-00

The Wide Field Camera 3 (WFC3) instrument on the Hubble Space Telescope has provided an abundance of exoplanet spectra over the years. These spectra have enabled analysis studies using atmospheric retrievals to constrain the properties of these objects. However, follow-up observations from the JWST have called into question some of the results from these older datasets, and highlighted the need to properly understand the degeneracies associated with retrievals of WFC3 spectra. In this study, we perform atmospheric retrievals of 38 transmission spectra from WFC3 and use model comparison to determine the complexity required to fit the data. We explore the effect of retrieving system parameters such as the stellar radius and planet's surface gravity, and thoroughly investigate the degeneracies between individual model parameters - specifically the temperature, abundance of water, and cloud-top level. We focus on three case studies (HD 209458b, WASP-12b, and WASP-39b) in an attempt to diagnose some of the issues with these retrievals, in particular the low retrieved temperatures when compared to the equilibrium values. Our study advocates for the careful consideration of parameter degeneracies when interpreting retrieval results, as well as the importance of wider wavelength coverage to break these degeneracies, in agreement with previous studies. The combination of data from multiple instruments, as well as analysis from multiple data reductions and retrieval codes, will allow us to robustly characterize the atmosphere of these exoplanets.

High-resolution Doppler-resolved spectroscopy has presented new opportunities for studying the atmospheres of exoplanets. While the 'classical' cross-correlation approach has proven to be efficient at finding atmospheric species, it is unable to perform direct atmospheric retrievals. Recent work has shown that retrievals are possible using a direct likelihood evaluation or likelihood 'mappings'. The unique aspect of high-resolution retrievals is that the data-processing methods required to remove the stellar and telluric lines also distort the underlying exoplanet's signal and therefore the forward model must be pre-processed to match this filtering. This was the key remaining limitation in our previously published framework. This paper directly addresses this by introducing a simple and fast model-filtering technique that can replicate the processing performed by algorithms such as SYSREM and PCA. This enables retrievals to be performed without having to perform expensive injection and pre-processing steps for every model. We show that we can reliably constrain quantitative measures of the atmosphere from transmission spectra including the temperature-pressure profile, relative abundances, planetary velocities, and rotational broadening parameters. Finally, we demonstrate our framework using UVES transmission spectroscopy of WASP-121b. We constrain the temperature-pressure profile and relative abundances of Fe, Cr, and V to be log<SUB>10</SUB>(χ<SUB>Fe</SUB>/χ<SUB>Cr</SUB>) = 1.66 ± 0.28, log<SUB>10</SUB>(χ<SUB>Fe</SUB>/χ<SUB>V</SUB>) = 3.78 ± 0.29, and log<SUB>10</SUB>(χ<SUB>Fe</SUB>/χ<SUB>Mg</SUB>) = -1.26 ± 0.60. The relative abundances are consistent with solar values, with the exception of Fe/Mg, where the large Mg abundance is probably explained by the escaping atmosphere of WASP-121b that is not accounted for in our atmospheric model.

Our combined spectrum displays an optical slope, which our models fit with opacity from scattering aerosols—either small-particle condensate clouds or photochemical hazes—though we cannot completely rule out the broad wings of Na or the effects of stellar contamination. Future observations are necessary to disentangle these effects.
